correctness.rationale: For p^a||A with valuation e_p(B)<a, exponent e_p is fixed. Multiplicativity gives J|tau. If J odd, all forced exponents are even; the explicit auxiliary square E (fixed exponents e_p and 2a at nonfixed p|A), CRT and Dirichlet yield a prime q outside E with E*q=B (mod A), so tau(Eq)=2 (mod4), disproving universal divisibility. If J=2 (mod4), exactly one forced exponent is 1 (mod4), all other forced exponents even; a term with tau=2 (mod4) is exactly p*t^2, giving the stated solvability iff. For A=8p^2,B=8beta+1, p||B supplies p-1 candidates; odd t has t^2=1 (mod8), so p!=1 (mod8) precludes exception, otherwise half the units fail quadratic solvability mod p. This proves cardinality for all odd primes; independently checked all A<=42 against positive terms and p=109 exact 108, with direct finite checks distinguished from infinite proof.
